methodology.title: How predictions are calculated
methodology.step1Desc: Elo is a rating system — originally invented for chess — that measures team strength purely from match results. Beating a stronger team earns more points; losing to a weaker team costs more. Unlike FIFA ranking, which uses a separate formula and is influenced by which matches a team chooses to play, Elo is a consistent mathematical record of head-to-head performance over time. In this model, a 400-point Elo gap translates to roughly 0.8 extra expected goals per game. A team with a higher Elo than their opponent starts with a scoring advantage, even if their FIFA rank is lower.
methodology.step2Desc: Once the tournament starts, attack strength, defence quality, and recent form (W/D/L) are factored in. These multiply the base λ — a team scoring well gets a boost, a team conceding heavily gets a penalty.
methodology.step3Desc: Red cards from previous matches result in automatic 1-match bans. A team with a suspended player gets a 0.92x multiplier on their expected goals, reflecting the reduced squad strength.
methodology.step4Desc: The two teams' λ values are fed into a Dixon-Coles Poisson model to generate a score matrix. Summing the probabilities gives us the chance of home win, draw, or away win (90 minutes).
methodology.step5Desc: When available, betting odds from multiple bookmakers are converted to implied probabilities (after removing the bookmaker margin). These are blended with the model's probabilities: 75% model + 25% market. This improves calibration by incorporating expert and quantitative consensus.
